graphperf: html is a one-item flex column, not a grid — WebKit's grid track sizing ran over body on every root layout; explicit minmax(0,1fr) tracks (7e7aa2ab) got back only 1 ms of testvault tabsw_note (9.25 vs v0.6.1 6.25, N=10 tabswF). flex-basis 0 + min-height 0 sizes body from html alone; same stretch-minus-margin noscroll geometry

graphperf: html's one grid cell is explicit, minmax(0,1fr) both ways — implicit 'auto' tracks take body's max-content contribution, so every root layout (a note tab switch) ran an intrinsic pass over the whole app first (testvault tabsw_note N=10: fc780bc7 8.5 -> c1e569ce 10.25 ms, v0.6.1 7.0, tabswN); same cell, same noscroll geometry

graphperf: graph_open_settle carries sg = click -> startGraph ms — since aa2367c3 a local graph's settle clock starts at the click (cmdLocalGraph), v0.6.1's at startGraph; the code between them (cmdLocalGraph/flushSave/splitWith) is unchanged, so the A/B subtracts sg to compare like with like

graphperf: body static again, html sizes it (one-cell grid, height 100%) — an absolute body still cost idle CPU after typing on the big vault (WebKitWebProcess 760-850 -> 1000-1160 ms/10s, gidleB1/B2); same noscroll geometry, no positioned body

graphperf: afterPaint waits two frames — the gg first frame's step() runs synchronously before the tab_switch span queues its paint rAF, so one rAF + setTimeout landed updateTitle() + perf.flush() inside that span's layout_ms (fixab3: layout 2 -> 5-9 ms, tabsw_gg x1.21)
